scenarios.name: 01-baseline
scenarios.description: Reference topology: 1 mixed connection, 1 channel, 1 publisher, 1 consumer. Constant workload across all scenarios: 1000000 total messages, 64 bytes each.

scenarios.name: 02-publishers-up
scenarios.description: Increase publishers only: 64 publishers, 1 consumer, still 1 mixed connection/channel. Publisher side is over-provisioned, so the single consumer/connection is the expected bottleneck.

scenarios.name: 03-consumers-up
scenarios.description: Increase consumers only: 64 consumers, 1 publisher, still 1 mixed connection/channel. Consumer side is over-provisioned, so the single publisher/connection is the expected bottleneck.

scenarios.name: 04-both-up
scenarios.description: Increase both publishers and consumers: 64 publishers and 64 consumers on 1 mixed connection/channel. The single connection/channel is the expected bottleneck.

scenarios.name: 05-publisher-conns-up
scenarios.description: Keep 64 publishers and 64 consumers, increase connections for publishers only: 16 publish-only connections/channels and 1 consume-only connection/channel. Consumer connection/channel is the expected bottleneck.

scenarios.name: 06-consumer-conns-up
scenarios.description: Keep 64 publishers and 64 consumers, increase connections for consumers only: 1 publish-only connection/channel and 16 consume-only connections/channels. Publisher connection/channel is the expected bottleneck.

scenarios.name: 07-both-conns-up
scenarios.description: Keep 64 publishers and 64 consumers, increase connections for both: 16 publish-only and 16 consume-only connections/channels. Both sides are provisioned; the broker's single exchange/queue dispatch is the expected bottleneck.
